ApiKeyScope.description: Scope granted to an API key. Parent scopes grant broad access; for example, `read` grants all read endpoints and `write` grants all write endpoints. Child scopes such as `read::block_trade_accept`, `read::portfolio_balance`, `write::trade`, `write::transfer`, `write::fcm_risk` (FCM subtrader creation, trading blocks, daily premium caps, and margin caps), and `write::block_trade_accept` grant only their specific endpoint group and can be granted without the parent scope.

ApiKeyType.description: Signature algorithm of an API key pair. `rsa` - 2048-bit RSA; requests are signed with RSA-PSS SHA-256. `ed25519` - Ed25519 (RFC 8032) signatures over the same pre-sign text, with lower client-side signing cost. Defaults to `rsa` when omitted from a generate request, for compatibility with existing clients.

BucketLimit.description:
Token-bucket budget for one rate-limit bucket. Each request deducts
tokens equal to its endpoint cost; the bucket refills at refill_rate
tokens per second up to bucket_capacity. A request is allowed if the
bucket holds enough tokens to cover its cost; otherwise the request
is rejected with HTTP 429.

refill_rate.description: Tokens added to the bucket per second.

bucket_capacity.description:
Maximum tokens the bucket can hold. When equal to refill_rate the
bucket holds one second of budget; larger values represent burst
headroom that idle clients accumulate and can spend in a single
pulse (e.g. write buckets at non-Basic tiers hold two seconds of
budget).

outcome_side.description:
The outcome side this order is positioned for. buy-yes and sell-no produce 'yes'; buy-no and sell-yes produce 'no'.

`outcome_side` describes directional exposure only; it does not change the order's price. An order at price `p` with `outcome_side=no` is matched by an order at the same price `p` with `outcome_side=yes` — both parties trade at the same price, just on opposite directions.

`outcome_side` and `book_side` will become the canonical way to determine order direction. The legacy `action`, `side`, and `is_yes` fields will be deprecated in a future release — please migrate to these new fields.

book_side.description:
Same directional bit as outcome_side in book vocabulary. 'bid' is equivalent to outcome_side 'yes'; 'ask' is equivalent to outcome_side 'no'.

`outcome_side` and `book_side` will become the canonical way to determine order direction. The legacy `action`, `side`, and `is_yes` fields will be deprecated in a future release — please migrate to these new fields.

outcome_side.description:
The outcome side this fill positioned the user for. buy-yes and sell-no produce 'yes'; buy-no and sell-yes produce 'no'.

`outcome_side` describes directional exposure only; it does not change the fill's price. A fill at price `p` with `outcome_side=no` is matched against an order at the same price `p` with `outcome_side=yes` — both parties trade at the same price, just on opposite directions.

`outcome_side` and `book_side` will become the canonical way to determine fill direction. The legacy `action` and `side` fields will be deprecated in a future release — please migrate to these new fields.

book_side.description:
Same directional bit as outcome_side in book vocabulary. 'bid' is equivalent to outcome_side 'yes'; 'ask' is equivalent to outcome_side 'no'.

`outcome_side` and `book_side` will become the canonical way to determine fill direction. The legacy `action` and `side` fields will be deprecated in a future release — please migrate to these new fields.

orderbook_fp.description: Orderbook with fixed-point contract counts (fp) in all price levels.

id.description: Unique identifier for this fee change

event_ticker.description: Event ticker this fee change applies to

anyOf.description: New fee type override for the event. When null, the event clears any prior override and falls back to the parent series' fee structure.
New fee multiplier override for the event. When null, the event clears any prior override and falls back to the parent series' fee multiplier.

markets.description: Data for the markets in this event. This field is deprecated in favour of the "markets" field inside the event. Which will be filled with the same value if you use the query parameter "with_nested_markets=true".

image_url.description: A path to an image that represents this market.

color_code.description: The color code for the market.

image_url.description: A path to an image that represents this event.

featured_image_url.description: A path to an image that represents the image of the featured market.

market_details.description: Metadata for the markets in this event.

settlement_sources.description: A list of settlement sources for this event.

anyOf.description: Event competition.
Event scope, based on the competition.

forecast_history.description: Array of forecast percentile data points over time.

event_ticker.description: The event ticker this forecast is for.

end_period_ts.description: Unix timestamp for the inclusive end of the forecast period.

period_interval.description: Length of the forecast period in minutes.

percentile_points.description: Array of forecast values at different percentiles.

series_ticker.description: Unique identifier for the series this event belongs to.

sub_title.description: Shortened descriptive title for the event.

collateral_return_type.description:
Collateral-return netting type for this event: `MECNET` for mutually exclusive markets, `DIRECNET` for directional netting, or an empty string for no collateral-return netting.
Netting applies within this event, not across all events in its series, and also requires netting to be enabled for the trading account or subtrader.
Use `with_nested_markets=true` to retrieve the markets associated with each event.

mutually_exclusive.description:
True when `collateral_return_type` is `MECNET`: at most one market in this event can resolve to 'yes'.
False for both `DIRECNET` and an empty collateral-return type. A false value does not mean collateral-return netting is unavailable. Use `collateral_return_type` to distinguish these cases.

category.description: Event category (deprecated, use series-level category instead).

anyOf.description: The specific date this event is based on. Only filled when the event uses a date strike (mutually exclusive with strike_period).
The time period this event covers (e.g., 'week', 'month'). Only filled when the event uses a period strike (mutually exclusive with strike_date).

markets.description: Array of markets associated with this event. Only populated when 'with_nested_markets=true' is specified in the request.

anyOf.description: Additional metadata for the event.
The official sources used for the determination of markets within this event. Methodology is defined in the rulebook.

last_updated_ts.description: Timestamp of when this event's metadata was last updated.

anyOf.description: Fee type override for this event. When present, takes precedence over the series-level fee for this event's markets.
Fee multiplier override for this event. Paired with fee_type_override.

frequency.description: Description of the frequency of the series. There is no fixed value set here, but will be something human-readable like weekly, daily, one-off.

title.description: Title describing the series. For full context use you should use this field with the title field of the events belonging to this series.

category.description: Category is the primary category of this series.

categories.description: Categories is the list of discovery categories for this series. The `category` filter on Get Series List matches any entry in this list. May be empty.

anyOf.description: Tags specifies the subjects that this series relates to, multiple series from different categories can have the same tags.
SettlementSources specifies the official sources used for the determination of markets within the series. Methodology is defined in the rulebook.

contract_url.description: ContractUrl provides a direct link to the original filing of the contract which underlies the series.

contract_terms_url.description: ContractTermsUrl is the URL to the current terms of the contract underlying the series.

anyOf.description: Internal product metadata of the series.

fee_type.description: FeeType is a string representing the series' fee structure. Fee structures can be found at https://kalshi.com/docs/kalshi-fee-schedule.pdf. 'quadratic' is described by the General Trading Fees Table, 'quadratic_with_maker_fees' is described by the General Trading Fees Table with maker fees described in the Maker Fees section, 'quadratic_with_combo_maker_fees' is the same maker-fee structure with a 0.5 maker multiplier instead of 0.25, 'flat' is described by the Specific Trading Fees Table.

fee_multiplier.description: FeeMultiplier is a floating point multiplier applied to the fee calculations.

anyOf.description: AdditionalProhibitions is a list of additional trading prohibitions for this series.

volume_fp.description: String representation of the total number of contracts traded across all events in this series.

last_updated_ts.description: Timestamp of when this series' metadata was last updated.
